goal: Research the state of agentic coding loops in 2026: identify the best end-to-end build processes using AI agents, where human checkpoints belong, and whether multi-model orchestration outperforms single-model loops for efficiency.
background: Producing a synthesis answer requires concrete evidence. Acceptance criteria: (1) name at least 3 distinct agentic loop patterns (e.g., plan-do-review, research/analyze/clarify/write/review pipelines, swarm orchestration, competitive implementation, ReAct-style, reflexion/critique loops) with strengths and weaknesses; (2) give an explicit answer on where human checkpoints belong (planning approval, work-order acceptance, mid-execution review, code review, merge/deploy gate) with rationale; (3) take a reasoned position on multi-model vs single-model efficiency, including conditions under which each wins across cost, latency, bias diversity, and judging overhead; (4) cover vendor patterns (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google) and open-source frameworks (LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, swarm-style) and notable agentic CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Aider, Devin-style) where relevant. Cite sources where possible. Output is industry research — no local codebase context is required.
